title: Gradient & intercept in context
examples: How do I know if the gradient is positive or negative?
What do the units of the gradient mean when I am dealing with time?
Can the gradient be zero in a real-life problem?

explain.say: Today we look at gradient in a real situation. The gradient shows the rate of change. It tells us how fast one thing changes compared to another.

draw.text: Gradient = change in y / change in x

explain.say: Think about a journey on a map. The gradient is the steepness of the path. We measure this using units for both parts.

draw.text: Units matter for rate of change.

explain.say: If the vertical axis is distance in metres, and the horizontal axis is time in minutes, the gradient is metres per minute. This is the unit for speed.
Consider a car journey where the distance is plotted against time. A gradient of two metres per minute means the car is moving up two metres every minute.

faq.q: What does a positive gradient mean in a real problem?
faq.a: A positive gradient means that as the horizontal value increases, the vertical value also increases. For example, if the gradient is positive, the object is rising or increasing.
asks: What does a positive slope mean?
When is the rate of change positive?

faq.q: What does a negative gradient tell me?
faq.a: A negative gradient means that as the horizontal value increases, the vertical value decreases. This suggests the object is falling or decreasing in value.
asks: How do I know if something is decreasing?
What does a negative gradient represent?

faq.q: Why are the units so important for the gradient?
faq.a: The units tell you exactly what the rate of change is. You must divide the units of the vertical axis by the units of the horizontal axis.
asks: Do I just divide the units?
What are the units of speed using a graph?

faq.a: The y-intercept is the value of the vertical axis when the horizontal axis is zero. It is the starting point of the process shown.
asks: What is the starting value on the graph?
Where does the line cross the vertical axis?

faq.a: Yes, a gradient of zero means there is no change in the vertical value, even if the horizontal value changes. This shows a constant level.
asks: What does a flat line mean?

facts: The gradient is the ratio of the change in the vertical axis to the change in the horizontal axis.
If the vertical axis is distance and the horizontal axis is time, the gradient represents speed.
A positive gradient indicates a rate of increase.
A negative gradient indicates a rate of decrease.

quiz.say: A graph plots the height of a balloon over time. The gradient is -5 metres per minute. What does this mean?

options.show: The balloon is sinking at a rate of five metres every minute.
options.say: The balloon is sinking at a rate of five metres every minute.

options.show: The balloon is rising at five metres every minute.
options.say: The balloon is rising at five metres every minute.

options.show: The balloon is sinking at five metres every minute squared.
options.say: The balloon is sinking at five metres every minute squared.

options.show: The balloon is at a constant height of five metres.
options.say: The balloon is at a constant height of five metres.

quiz.why: The negative sign shows the height is decreasing, and the units tell us the rate is five metres per minute.

wrong.1: This ignores the negative sign, which shows the height is falling.
wrong.2: This incorrectly changes the units from metres per minute to metres per minute squared.
wrong.3: The gradient shows the rate of change, not the current height.

quiz.say: A graph shows the cost of fuel over distance. The gradient is 0.10 pounds per kilometre. What is the unit of the gradient?
quiz.why: The gradient is calculated by dividing the change in cost (pounds) by the change in distance (kilometres).

wrong.0: The gradient must have units that show a rate of change, not just two separate units.
wrong.1: This adds an extra unit that is not related to the simple rate of change.
wrong.2: This reverses the ratio, incorrectly suggesting distance is changing over cost.

quiz.say: A graph shows a runner's position. The gradient is positive. Which statement best describes the runner?

options.show: The runner is moving towards the starting point.
options.say: The runner is moving towards the starting point.

options.show: The runner is moving away from the starting point.
options.say: The runner is moving away from the starting point.

quiz.why: A positive gradient means both values are increasing together, which describes movement away from the start.

wrong.0: Moving towards the start would result in a negative gradient.
wrong.1: Standing still would result in a gradient of zero.
wrong.2: The graph only shows movement along the plotted axes, not sideways.
